Hi Alyssa — thanks for sending this over. I reviewed the draft and put inline comments in a redline (see attached PDF). High-level position and evidence we can provide below.

High-level positions:
- Service provider designation: Redwood will accept the "service provider" role for US-state addenda (CPRA/CCPA). We confirm we will not "sell" Personal Information as defined in those statutes. We typically mirror that with contractual language that restricts retention / use to the purpose of providing the service.

- Subprocessors: attached is our living subprocessor list (Redwood_Subprocessors_20261101.csv). We ask customers to accept standard notice + consent process for subprocessors; for certain controlled customers we can agree to a 7-day notice and objection right for new subprocessors.

- Cross-border transfers & controls: for hosted API customers Redwood operates across cloud regions and may process data in the US and other regions. For US-state compliance this is generally acceptable, but if DataTrust requires US-only processing we can discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options (these support region locks and customer-managed KMS). For exports out of the EU we rely on SCCs/appropriate transfer mechanisms for qualifying customers — let us know if you need those for this agreement.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (we can provide an attested copy under an NDA), penetration test summary, and our subprocessor registry link: https://status.redwood.ai/subprocessors. SOC 2 link: https://downloads.redwood.ai/reports/SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf

Requested clarifications to your draft:
1) Section 3 (Data Transfers): please clarify whether you need a contractual export mechanism (SCCs) for US→EU flows or simply a commitment to comply with export rules.
2) Section 5 (Subprocessors): we propose to accept the objection period of 7 business days for high-risk subprocessors; otherwise notice and standard terms.

Attachments included: Redwood_Subprocessors_20261101.csv (current roster), SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf, and a redline "Redwood_US-State-Addendum-redline.pdf" with suggested edits (mainly limited to preserving service-provider obligations and removing overly broad audit or deletion timelines that would be operationally infeasible).

Next steps:
- If you want, we'll produce both a clean Redwood US addendum and a marked-up copy of your draft. We can also schedule a 30-min call with Karthik to run through the transfer questions and the residency/KMS options.

Thanks,
